scenarios.description: A release is prepared after Framework Source changes.
scenarios.expected: Only Framework Source is edited. tools/build_release.py validates Source and generates the disposable Project Runtime artifact plus release metadata.

scenarios.description: A normal implementation, debugging, review, or project-navigation response is produced.
scenarios.expected: Codex and Claude universal contracts lead with the result/useful action, preserve correctness/safety/completeness over brevity, Standalone inherits the behavior through generated composition, and the Personal repository router does not duplicate the universal block.

scenarios.description: A non-trivial coding task requires repository grounding, environment setup, implementation, validation, debugging, or waiting on a long-running command.
scenarios.expected: Codex and Claude batch independent reconnaissance and bound inspection reads; implementation probes knowable prerequisites together; validation stops after required evidence is sufficient; repeated same-cause failures pivot the hypothesis/approach; long-running commands avoid frequent empty polling. None of these rules weakens correctness, acceptance criteria, security gates, or required tests.

scenarios.description: Framework maintainers compare an execution-efficiency candidate against a baseline using real agent runs.
scenarios.expected: Baseline and candidate runs are paired under controlled conditions, efficiency claims use paired deltas with quality gates, and the measurement protocol/schema/analyzer remain Framework Source-only rather than becoming Project Runtime dependencies.

scenarios.description: A discovery benchmark or trace reveals a repeatable waste pattern and maintainers test a behavioral optimization.
scenarios.expected: One experiment isolates one primary hypothesis/change, paired evidence must pass the quality gate before KEEP is allowed, decided records are terminal so MODIFY creates a linked new experiment, and release verification rejects inconsistent registry/lifecycle/evidence state.

scenarios.description: Codex or Claude operates with Progressive Context while a task may require architecture choice, implementation/testing, documentation accuracy, or completion reporting.
scenarios.expected: Universal adapters delegate project-specific behavior to Progressive; architecture options are evidence-driven rather than fixed filler; substantial testing can add a bounded dev-only framework; implementation-coupled docs update automatically while governance remains gated; final reports are result-first with Manual check only when useful.

scenarios.description: A new project or change request needs enough planning for correctness without generating unnecessary specification work.
scenarios.expected: The agent selects the smallest sufficient DIRECT/FOCUSED/FULL depth from uncertainty, architectural reach, risk, reversibility, and contract impact rather than size alone; new projects persist the selected depth, later changes re-evaluate it independently, and the protocol is available in Project Runtime. Lower planning depth never bypasses required engineering, safety, acceptance, or validation work.

scenarios.description: Framework maintainers add or change a Skill without changing ordinary routing behavior.
scenarios.expected: Every canonical Skill declares automatic, explicit, or both activation in frontmatter; the metadata remains in the task-triggered Skill layer rather than expanding always-loaded instructions.

scenarios.description: Framework maintainers or release automation need one complete static/integrity verification entrypoint without duplicating the check sequence across CI, release, and Skills.
scenarios.expected: tools/gate.py is the single Framework Source verification orchestrator; CI, release, and workflow-audit delegate to it, child validators remain independently executable, Project Runtime keeps its separate local audit surface, and a gate PASS is not presented as empirical model-quality evidence.
